subject.title: Matrix DM session-key lowercasing collides case-distinct MXIDs, sharing one peer's DM transcript with another under per-peer scope

question: Should the security fix preserve only Matrix direct peer IDs now, or also enroll Signal direct peer IDs in the shared case-preservation registry?
rationale: The Matrix source path and DM isolation contract are clear, but widening the same registry to Signal direct changes a security-sensitive session-key boundary without direct Signal identity-contract proof in this review.

options.title: Fix Matrix direct first
options.body: Preserve Matrix direct MXID case now and leave Signal direct unchanged until a focused Signal direct-ID contract and regression proof exists.

options.title: Enroll Matrix and Signal direct
options.body: Preserve both Matrix and Signal direct IDs, but require explicit proof that Signal direct IDs are case-sensitive opaque principals before merge.

options.title: Wait for live homeserver proof
options.body: Defer implementation until a live permissive Matrix homeserver demonstrates the full inbound-to-transcript-load leak, trading speed for stronger runtime proof.

recommendation.title: Fix Matrix direct first
recommendation.body: Preserve Matrix direct MXID case now and leave Signal direct unchanged until a focused Signal direct-ID contract and regression proof exists.

likelyOwner.reason: He carried the recent maintainer fixups and validation around Matrix session-key alias, delivery, and migration safety in the same code path.
